newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court pulls plug on Tapie's screen stardom.
newsitem.headline: French court pulls plug on Tapie's screen stardom.

text.p: A French court refused on Thursday to grant semi-liberty to jailed bankrupt businessman and ex-soccer boss Bernard Tapie, wrecking his bid to star in a second film, justice sources said.
The sources said a commission in Aix-en-Provence in southern France threw out the request, filed by Tapie on Wednesday from the Luynes jail where he is serving a term for rigging a match.
Tapie had sought permission to spend his days out of jail, and his nights behind bars, to allow him to star in a new film.

The former parliamentarian, cabinet minister and chairman of Marseille soccer club last year took centre-screen in Claude Lelouche's popular "Hommes Femmes: Mode d'Emploi" (Men, Women, Instructions for Use), which was filmed while Tapie faced a host of lawsuits.

Tapie, who says he is the innocent victim of a political witchhunt in France, has been in jail since February 3, serving an eight-month sentence for rigging a league soccer match between Marseille and Valenciennes in 1993.
